sections: How step pruning bounds tree growth

blocks.md: This lesson covers the book's section on **Bounded Search**. Read the excerpt, then test yourself below.

blocks.source: Vol III, Test-Time Compute, § Bounded Search
blocks.md: The repair agent now holds several partial candidates at once, some freshly revised and some untouched. At each step it can sample a fresh patch from the root, extend an existing partial candidate by one segment, or run a diagnostic probe to separate competing explanations. Every choice draws from the same task budget while creating different scheduling dependencies. A probe that gates the next code extension sits on the critical path. Independent candidate extensions can run in parallel across worker slots.

blocks.title: What the section covers
blocks.md:
In the book this section runs through:

- Where each search structure prunes
- How step pruning bounds tree growth
- Isolating workspaces across search branches
- Accounting for the whole search
- Reserving budget before admitting work
- When to stop searching early

blocks.prompt: Think first: In two or three sentences, explain why Search tree pruning matters for the system this section describes.
blocks.md: Compare your answer with the book's claim: A step check that rejects a fraction r of b children gives an effective branching factor b(1-r), so a tree stays finite on its own only when r > 1-1/b and otherwise needs hard caps.

questions.q: The section **Bounded Search** develops one of the chapter's claims. Which one?
options: Voting and learned ranking both return the best failure from a defective pool, so only selection by a check the candidate cannot modify justifies returning a candidate instead of abstaining.
A search tracks money, non-interchangeable work, wall time, and peak live state in separate accounts and reserves each request's maximum charge before dispatch, releasing it only on settlement.
Before admitting more work, apply hard ceilings, then satisficing, then marginal stopping, and an exhausted budget returns unresolved or escalates rather than lowering the acceptance threshold.
A step check that rejects a fraction r of b children gives an effective branching factor b(1-r), so a tree stays finite on its own only when r > 1-1/b and otherwise needs hard caps.
